text: I just got a Mac mini with an M5 Pro (base CPU config) and 48GB of unified memory. I want to run as much AI locally as makes sense, but it's hard to separate what actually works day to day from benchmark hype. What I'd like to do: Questions: Real tokens/sec numbers and "this was a waste of time" stories are especially welcome. Qwen3.8-27B is by far the best coding model runnable locally. However, it will be difficult to hold a long context window, and forget about running multiple coding sessions in parallel. It's also going to be annoyingly slow for interactive work. It can be useful if you give it chores to do in the background or overnight. It can be useful as a secondary model like advisor role in oh-my-pi. Unfortunately, other models smaller than 27B are too dumb for coding (in serious projects you'll get more bugs than help from them). 4-bit quants are optimal for small RAM budget. Going lower starts breaking the models and higher quants give you diminishing results. gemma4-e4b is small and pretty fast, and works fine as a lossy wikipedia and a smarter regex (searching and summarization where accuracy isn't critical), but don't let it edit anything that you want to keep. Comfy stuff tends to fit easily in 48GB, but it's a bit slow (most workflows are designed for nvidia cards with less VRAM and more raw power). I've got 48GB M3 Max and 96GB M5 Ultra. The 96GB is still barely usable for real coding, and financially doesn't make sense compared to Deepseek 4.1 Flash that's smarter, 4x faster than anything I can run, and doesn't OOM when I run more than a couple things at once. I have the same hardware as you and I've been using MLX-LM with Qwen3.6-27B 6bit quant. My setup is a vibe-coded local server that just wires together a bunch of different components with a web UI. It's fairly fast in terms of token output, but noticeably worse than claude at coding. It can handle routine tasks and I've been using it to scan my codebase for bugs. Low-powered models work pretty well for finding bugs if you make them verify the bug is real. I was also using it for some voice assistant stuff (with a separate speech-to-text and text-to-speech setup) and it was pretty good at handling natural language questions and using tools accordingly (turn the lights on, play music, etc.). I got it to a point where the latency was extremely low and it felt really responsive. As for image generation, the version I was able to get running on my home setup was drastically worse than the big company offerings and I didn't really have much use for it, so I abandoned that part. My local setup: M1 Max 64GB, LM Studio, pi, and OrbStack for isolation. I get about 60 tps from Gemma 4 26B A4B QAT and prefer MLX if available for a small speed increase. I use this setup when I want complete privacy. Or I'll use it to hear my fan spin up and get a feel for what's happening under the hood, details an API would hide. That I pay my own power bill is satisfying for part but not all of the ethics problem. I look forward to a local setup being good enough for most anybody, so we can in some form give back to the commons what we took. For now I'm constrained by models being either too dumb to depend on or too slow on this chip to wait for. But they are much smarter per time than two years ago when I first explored this. For general questions, I'm happy enough with Siri AI. It's fine for a first try and that's often plenty. And local + PCC is usually private enough. For automated coding tasks whose results I'll depend on to be good, I'd go back to the two major players and get a subscription again. I don't have one today, but I'd get whichever is not on tap at work.
